title: Representational Duplication / API Representation Leaks
pattern: Knowledge of an external API's response schema fields is duplicated and scattered across multiple independent methods, rather than being encapsulated in a single parsing interface.
why_bad: It creates multiple DRY violations. If the external API updates its response format (e.g., changes `"name"` to `"full_name"`), multiple independent client methods break simultaneously, complicating upgrades.
detection: The same API schema paths, JSON key literals, or payload structures are referenced across multiple separate methods.
counterexample: Standard parsing macros or serialization templates that group mappings in a single localized definition.
fix:
Parse the external payload into a single, dedicated type at the system boundary, isolating external schema details from the rest of the application.
```rust
#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct ExternalUser {
    name: String,
    age: u32,
}
```
source: *Andrew Hunt & David Thomas - The Pragmatic Programmer, Chapter 2 (A Pragmatic Approach), "REPRESENTATIONAL DUPLICATION"*
